positions.as_written: Learn the prominences as a set of offsets.
Identify the epicondyle, work to the adductor tubercle, then to the gastrocnemius tubercle, and the attachments are then located rather than hunted.
Identify all three prominences before placing anything.
Use the semimembranosus tubercle as the posteromedial tibial reference, because it is bone and the joint line is an estimate.
Plan fixation points together rather than in sequence.
Identify the three prominences and mark them before any fixation, because the field is too small to correct an error by eye.
Plan the graft positions for both structures before placing either, since they compete for bone.
Set tension at the angle each structure is tight, not at a single angle for the construct.
Warn about the saphenous branch before operating.
Preserve vascularity in tissue intended to heal.
Consider the chronic medial knee as a length problem rather than a continuity problem.
